descriptive_title: Grade 1 Mathematics: Algebra (Modelling) — Mathematical Modelling at the Sugar Bush (C4)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.C4: apply the process of mathematical modelling to represent, analyse, make predictions, and provide insight into real-life situations

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 1 unit on mathematical modelling, framed around the Canadian sugar bush — Maple the Maple Tree mascot and Sap Sam the Sap Collector. Children walk through the modelling cycle: identify a real-life situation, ask a question, collect data, build a model, use it to predict, reflect on accuracy. The week culminates in children applying the modelling cycle to their own real-life situation.
unit_learning_goal: Children will apply the mathematical modelling cycle (situation → question → data → model → predict → reflect) to a real-life situation.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Mathematical modelling starts with a real-life situation. We pay attention to what's happening and ask questions.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can describe a real-life situation and ask math questions about it.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Maple introduces the sugar bush; class brainstorms questions like 'how many trees?' 'how much sap?'

lesson_arc.big_idea: We collect data — count trees, measure tap holes — to feed our model.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can collect data to answer a math question about a real-life situation.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children count paper trees and predict how many taps; record on a chart.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We use the data to make predictions. If 1 tap fills 1 bucket, then 5 taps fill 5 buckets.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can use data to predict an outcome.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Sap Sam predicts: if 1 tap → 1 bucket, predict for 4, 6, 8 taps.

lesson_arc.big_idea: After predictions, we check our model against reality. Sometimes the model is off — we refine it.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can check my prediction against what really happens and adjust the model.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children compare predicted vs actual sap counts; refine the rule.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can model any real-life situation. Pick a topic from your life, ask a question, build a model.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can model a real-life situation from my own life.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children invent their own real-life modelling problem (recess game scores, snack distribution, etc.) and walk through the cycle.

recurring_characters.name: Maple the Maple Tree
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. A friendly maple tree mascot that stands at the sugar bush. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A maple tree character with a smiling face on the trunk, vibrant red-orange leaves, sugar tap on the side, syrup bucket below. Cheerful expression.

recurring_characters.name: Sap Sam the Collector
recurring_characters.role: The hardworking helper who collects sap. Anchors Lessons 2 and 3.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young person in a plaid coat and toque, carrying a sap bucket and a wooden tap. Friendly Canadian smile.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: A math representation of a real-life situation. The model helps us predict what will happen.
To say what we think will happen based on what we know.
Information we collect by counting, measuring, or observing.
Something that happens in the world we can ask math questions about.
To improve something. We refine our model when reality is different from our prediction.

assessment_strategy.diagnostic: Lesson 1: can the child describe a real-life situation and ask a math question about it?
assessment_strategy.formative: Lesson 2: data-collection accuracy. Lesson 3: prediction accuracy. Lesson 4: reflection-and-refinement.
assessment_strategy.summative: Lesson 5: child applies the full modelling cycle to their own real-life situation.

pedagogical_notes: C4 is the 'modelling' overall expectation — children walk through the modelling cycle multiple times.
The sugar bush is a quintessentially Canadian context — maple syrup is a strong cultural anchor.
Modelling is iterative — we EXPECT predictions to be off and refine them.
Capstone Lesson 5 invites children to model THEIR life — strongest engagement signal.
canadian_context_notes: Sugar bush season runs late February to early April in Ontario. Schools sometimes do field trips.
Maple trees, sap, syrup are uniquely Canadian symbols — Indigenous-origin technology.
Other real-life modelling contexts: ice fishing, hockey scores, recess weather.
